# Payment-risk model report (generated by `python -m ato.train`)

## What this does and does not show

- Data is **synthetic** (`ato/simulate.py`). There is no public labelled Indian UPI fraud data. We wrote both the scams and the detector, so results partly confirm our own assumptions. These numbers show the pipeline works and how the model behaves under missing signals, scammers who hide, and unseen scam types. They are **not** real-world precision/recall.
- Fraud prevalence in the simulation is far higher than in production. Friction rates (share of *legitimate* payments challenged) do not depend on prevalence; precision does (see the prevalence table).
- Test slice: days 120-150, 272,875 payments, 347 scam incidents across 14 types. Per-type rows have only a handful to a few dozen incidents, so read the ranges.

## Severity thresholds (friction budgets on legitimate validation payments)

| severity | max legit share |
|---|---|
| MEDIUM | 2% |
| HIGH | 0.3% |
| CRITICAL | 0.05% |

The budget is shared by all three heads (takeover, coached, payee): a payment reaches a level if ANY head is that surprised.

## Headline (test, HIGH = strong action: face check, wait/approval, or block)

| model | legit >= MEDIUM | legit >= HIGH | legit >= CRITICAL | incidents caught at HIGH [95% range] | first payment caught | rupees saved |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Full ML (3 heads)** | 1.6% | 0.2% | 0.0% | 89.6% [86.0%-92.4%] | 84.7% | 95.5% |
| Server-only ML | 1.6% | 0.2% | 0.0% | 89.3% [85.6%-92.2%] | 84.4% | 97.2% |
| Hand-written rules | 2.0% | 0.2% | 0.0% | 33.4% [28.7%-38.6%] | 23.3% | 51.7% |

## Shortcut check

A model that sees only WHICH values are missing (not the values) reaches test ROC-AUC 0.708 for fraud vs legit. Attackers legitimately have some different missingness (e.g. an attacker's phone may not run the SDK), so it is not 0.5, but a high value would mean the data leaks the label through missingness. An earlier simulator bug of this kind was caught by probing and fixed.

## Precision depends on how common fraud is (full model, HIGH)

| fraud share of payments | share of HIGH alerts that are real fraud |
|---|---|
| 0.01 | 82.1% |
| 0.001 | 31.2% |
| 0.0001 | 4.3% |
| 1e-05 | 0.5% |

Simulated test prevalence: 0.395%. Real UPI fraud is far rarer, so most HIGH alerts would land on genuine users unless the action is cheap. That is why the budget at HIGH is small and MEDIUM is only a prompt or warning.

Model scoring latency (three heads, one payment, model only): 16.9 ms.
